message.reasoning:
Let me evaluate against the rubric.

C1: Introduction identifies three ethical issues, links to engineering design, discusses organisational context ("design-process decision made by the organisation"), and stakeholders with Table 1. Excellent — 10.

C2: Balanced discussion — arguments for and against, conclusions with recommendations for multiple stakeholders (Rachel, management, health department, chip supplier, engineers). Excellent — 10.

C3: Compelling argument, logical structure, conclusion well supported. Excellent — 10.

C4: Research and evidence — 8 references, quantitative evidence (81 of 236 trusts, 19,000 appointments, $475M, $4.3B), qualitative. Excellent — 10.

C5: Structure, format, language — abstract, intro, body, conclusion, recommendations; two tables, one figure; IEEE references; fluent writing. Excellent — 10. Any issues? Minor: "Recommendations" section after conclusion is fine. Word count unknown but seems within limits. I'd give 10 or maybe 9? Levels only allow 10, 8, 6, 4, 0 — whole number within level range; Excellent is 10 only. Very good is 8. The report is very strong; visuals used competently, references extensive. Give 10.

Requirements: R1–R7 all met. R1: distinction between physical harm and data loss addressed. R2: ethical way to conduct business discussed, rule proposed. R3: trade-offs in Table 2 and discussion. R4: health department contract, WannaCry, hospitals. R5: stakeholders Table 1. R6: case studies, references. R7: recommendations.

Technical issues: minor — WannaCry was ransomware not hardware defect (student acknowledges). Intel charge $475M correct. VW $4.3B correct. Therac-25 six overdoses correct (actually six known accidents, some fatal). Stalk 1988 HBR correct. All fine.

Overall: excellent report.
